entities.summary:
The foreign minister is the head of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran and a member of the Cabinet. The office is currently held by Abbas Araghchi since 2024.

This position was established during the reign of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi in 1955, marking a significant shift towards modernizing Iran's diplomatic relations.

The foreign minister plays a crucial role in representing Iran's interests abroad, negotiating international agreements, and maintaining diplomatic relations with other countries. The current foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, has been instrumental in shaping Iran's foreign policy, particularly in the context of the Iran nuclear deal.

The legacy of the foreign minister can be seen in the establishment of diplomatic relations with other countries, the negotiation of international agreements, and the representation of Iran's interests on the global stage.
